questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit — the primary component of a computer that executes instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a volatile memory?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — it loses its contents when power is removed.

questions.question: What is the base of the binary number system?
questions.explanation: Binary uses base 2, meaning only digits 0 and 1 are used.

questions.question: Which data structure operates on a LIFO principle?
questions.explanation: A Stack operates on Last-In-First-Out (LIFO): the last element pushed is the first to be popped.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each iteration, giving O(log n) time complexity.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has the best average-case performance?
questions.explanation: Quick Sort has an average-case complexity of O(n log n), making it highly efficient in practice.

questions.question: What does OOP stand for?
questions.explanation: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming — a paradigm based on classes and objects.

questions.question: Which principle ensures a class has only one reason to change?
questions.explanation: The Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) states that a class should have only one reason to change.

questions.question: What is a closure in programming?
options: A function that captures variables from its enclosing scope
A way to close a file handle
questions.explanation: A closure is a function that retains access to variables from its lexical scope even after the outer function returns.
